messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: KV cache miss-rate spike detected for backbone-rope-pool (kv_cache_miss_rate=0.28 over 6m, p95_latency_tokens=430ms) — auto-escalation to oncall.

jordan (oncall): on it. seeing the alert. are we seeing customer errors or elevated 5xx?

maya (eng-sre): no increase in 5xx from the front doors, mostly tail latency and throughput drop on long-context paths (requests with rope.ntk > 1024). Grafana: https://graf.redwood/g/kvs/rope_pool?from=now-30m shows the miss spike correlates with continuous-batching backlog.

sam (runtime): initial read: a recent experimental sliding-window commit for YaRN/NTK prefetched more KV entries than we accounted for — KV cardinality jumped ~3.5x, causing mem-pressure and more cache evictions -> more cold misses -> larger batching + head-of-line latencies.

jordan (oncall): ok, mitigation plan? can we throttle prefetch or reduce sliding window briefly?

maya (eng-sre): yes, two fast options: 1) disable longrope prefetch flag for the pool (longrope.prefetch.enabled=false) as a kill-switch, 2) reduce continuous-batching.max_window_tokens from 2048 -> 512 to break up large batches. I'll prepare both.

sam (runtime): +1. reducing max_window_tokens will reduce per-batch memory and KV pressure. disabling prefetch is heavier but safest. recommend try batch size first to avoid full feature rollback.

rachel (support): are customers impacted? any big tenants hitting long-context today? I can draft a blast if there will be visible latency.

maya (eng-sre): quick customer check: internal tenant-telemetry shows top 5 tenants making long-context calls; only two have heavy NTK traffic — they will see p95->p99 latency bump if we do nothing. With batch-size reduction we expect latency for single-token responses to drop in 10-15m.

jordan (oncall): do the batch change first. maya, can you push a hotpatch to the config service? sam, be ready to flip the prefetch flag if it doesn't stabilize.

maya (eng-sre): preparing patch. patch diff:```yaml
- continuous_batching:
-   max_window_tokens: 2048
+ continuous_batching:
+   max_window_tokens: 512
``` Deploy plan: config-service -> canary to 5% rope-pool -> monitor 10m -> roll to 100% if stable.

maya (eng-sre): applying change now: `kubectl apply -f hotfixs/2063456789/batch-window.yaml --namespace=config`

deploy-bot: canary-deploy started for config hotfix (hotfixs/2063456789) — target: rope-pool canary 5% (10 pods).

maya (eng-sre): monitoring metrics: within 2m the kv_cache_miss_rate dropped from 28% -> 14% in the canary subset; p95 latency on canary decreased ~30ms.

sam (runtime): good sign. however global pool still shows miss-rate at ~22% because rollout not complete. if canary continues to look good, roll it.

jordan (oncall): proceed to 100% rollout. rachel, hold off on customer notification for now, just standby.

deploy-bot: rollout progressing -> 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% (approx 8m).

maya (eng-sre): rollout complete at 2063456950. global kv_cache_miss_rate now 9% and trending down. tail latency p95 down ~120ms from peak.

sam (runtime): watching evictions metric: eviction_rate decreased, memory pressure easing. I still see a small set of pods with higher GC churn — investigating whether those hosts had amplified YaRN prefetch previously.

jordan (oncall): do we still need to flip the prefetch flag?

maya (eng-sre): not yet. I want to let the current change stabilize for 15-20m. If evictions drop under threshold and latency stays low, we can avoid the feature rollback.

rachel (support): customer-impact update: internal monitoring shows no SLO breaches for 98% of tenants. Two heavy-NTK customers saw degraded p99 for a 12-minute window; I'll open a support ticket and ping their CSMs. Draft message ready if we need an external status.

sam (runtime): follow-up: I ran a quick heap profile on an affected pod; you can see the trace showing prefetch entries pinned due to sliding-window indexing:```text
heap: 1.8GB -> 3.9GB (before)
most-retained: rope/preload_buffers ~ 1.6GB
caller: yarn.slide_window_load()
``` We'll schedule a proper fix to guard prefetch cardinality.

maya (eng-sre): agreed — long-term action items: 1) add cardinality cap on rope.prefetch.window_entries (default 50k), 2) back-pressure when KV miss-rate rises above 10% (prevent further prefetch), 3) observability: add per-tenant NTK heatmap and prefetch budget alerts.

jordan (oncall): sounds good. create an incident tracking ticket with links and assign to sam + runtime team and maya for a postmortem. I'll update incident channel in 30m with final status.

deploy-bot: Canary hotfix (2063456789) succeeded.

maya (eng-sre): marking this stabilizing window. current metrics at 2063457020: kv_cache_miss_rate=0.07, p95_latency=210ms (down from 330ms peak), eviction_rate normalized.

rachel (support): support ticket created: #INC-8374, contacted affected customers and CSMs, they acknowledged. No external status update required at this point.

sam (runtime): filing follow-up RFC for prefetch safety nets (will link to ticket). Also triaging the PR that increased sliding-window default size — revert or add caps.

jordan (oncall): thanks all. keeping this thread open for 1 hour for any regressions. If nothing else, I'll mark incident tidy and we can put a short postmortem in postmortems/.

maya (eng-sre): note for the postmortem: root cause: change in sliding-window defaults increased prefetch cardinality, continuous-batching config amplified memory pressure -> cascade of evictions and miss amplification. Fix implemented: short-term reduce batch window; medium-term add prefetch caps and back-pressure; long-term improve load-shedding heuristics for NTK-heavy flows.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged as RECOVERED by jordan (oncall) at 2063457025.

jordan (oncall): closing thread, moving to postmortem drafting. great quick coordination everyone :thumbsup:
